chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Rehearsing and travelling to the Okeh studio
summary: She rehearsed at her pianist's room, including with Clarence Williams, and rode the el to the studio on 45th Street.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When you went to the Nest, did they have -- did people go in for breakfast dances, too? Or was it just matinee time?
Oh, I imagine -- I don't know whether they did, but I never did go.
You never did?

No, no. The only time I would go was just sometimes I'd go there ______ Saturday evening or Sunday evening, you know. But during the week, I wouldn't go. I was always working, I was always working, because I was getting my numbers down, rehearsing to myself, you know, and everything, and then ______. My piano player who was going to play with me, you know, he would have a piano and I would go to his room and we would rehearse, you know, and get songs down pat as much as we could ______, so when we went to recording office, we wouldn't take too much rehearsing.
So did you rehearse with Clarence
Williams? Oh, yes.
A lot?
Oh, yeah.
Now, if you lived up in Harlem, how did you go down -- where was the Okay Studio?
On 45th.
And how did you go down there?
I'd always get a cab or go on the el.
You went on the el?
(Unintelligible).
Remember how much that cost?
No, I don't remember how much the far was now. Used to always go on the el.
But you'd take a taxi sometimes?
Well, sometimes if it was raining or something like that, you know. But I --
You don't remember how much that cost?
I wouldn't know what it cost. My brother always paid for me. No, I wouldn't take no taxi because it cost too much money. I'd go on the el.
